title: A live stream wedges the fleet-wide server worker with no bound (pasted /live/ link, or a ticked live result)
what: The server executor downloads whatever the URL resolves to with no live-stream refusal and no wall-clock limit, and the worker reads cancel_requested only between clips. parse_url_list accepts /live/ links, a paste never passes the filter phase, and a search job's 'live or no duration' drop is a soft deselect the editor can overrule. yt-dlp records an ongoing live stream until it ends.
cost: One pasted 24/7 /live/ link holds the single fleet-wide worker indefinitely: every editor's jobs queue behind it, a .part grows ~3-4 GB/hour at 1080p (estimated) on the NAS, CANCEL is not read until the clip ends, and a container restart re-attaches (reset_stale_jobs keeps downloading jobs pending) unless cancel was pressed first. The companion is bounded by CLIP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 2 h; the server is not.
evidence: Read build_opts/download (no match_filter, no is_live check), _ID_PATHS includes 'live', _phase_download checks cancel/lease only per iteration, companion ytdl_executor.py:324 CLIP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. Not run against YouTube per the brief.
fix: Refuse live/upcoming in build_opts via a match_filter (!is_live & live_status != is_upcoming) with a clip-row note, and add a per-clip deadline plus a cancel check that aborts from the progress hook on the worker thread so the abort follows the normal _record_failure cleanup path; keeps the 'never torn down from another thread' rule.

title: The two executors' conversion step has drifted: the server's ffmpeg/ffprobe have no timeout and cannot be cancelled
what: The companion's edit-ready conversion uses Popen, a 3 h ceiling, a cancellable child and a tree kill; the server's vendored copy runs a blocking subprocess.run with no timeout, so a hung or very slow libx264 re-encode or ffprobe holds the single fleet-wide worker and a cancel waits for it. The encode runs in the dashboard container at full thread count with no nice/-threads cap.
cost: Every 1440p/2160p clip (VP9/AV1 only above 1080p) is a full crf-18 medium re-encode on the NAS CPU, tens of minutes per clip-hour (estimated); the worker is unavailable to every editor meanwhile, cancel is not honoured, and dashboard requests compete for CPU. A wedged ffmpeg is a worker wedged until restart.
evidence: Read both implementations side by side; ytdl_common is already the shared contract module and carries neither timeout.
fix: Move CLIP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS/CONVERT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS into ytdl_common for both sides; run the server's ffmpeg via Popen with a poll loop that also checks a cancel callable, kill on either, and reuse the existing unstage() failure path. Optionally cap -threads so the dashboard keeps a core.

title: Every download-phase poll re-fetches the whole manifest (296 KB for 400 candidates) to draw 40 rows, uncompressed, in hidden tabs too
what: While a job downloads, each tick fetches the 7 KB poll plus the full manifest (every candidate and column) only to read dl_state/dl_error of the selected rows. No visibilitychange handling anywhere in the SPA and no response gzip.
cost: Measured 296,156 bytes per manifest (400 candidates, 40 selected). A 30-minute 40-clip download at 5 s ticks = ~360 fetches = ~107 MB per open tab per job, over the tailnet for remote editors; doubles with a second or forgotten background tab.
evidence: Probe: real schema in a temp DB, manifest body built exactly as routes_api.manifest builds it (3.3 ms, 296 KB); read poll() and renderDownloads.
fix: Carry the dl_state != 'none' rows (about 6 KB for 40) in the poll response while downloading and drop the per-tick manifest fetch; keep the terminal-phase loadManifest. Skip or stretch ticks while document.hidden.

title: The poll never stops at terms_review and re-renders the checkbox list every tick
what: terms_review is a person-wait phase like ready_for_review, but polling continues at 5 s for as long as the tab is open and each tick rebuilds every checkbox row, losing keyboard focus and risking a click on a detached node.
cost: A review left open overnight is ~17,000 requests per tab per day, each 5-6 SQL statements on the dashboard's single process; ~350k/day at 20 editors with a parked tab each (estimated).
evidence: Read poll() stop set and renderTermReview.
fix: Stop polling at terms_review (the continue action can reschedule) or slow it to 30 s; render the list once per job and update only the count afterwards.

title: Filter and enrich phases commit once per row (927 ms vs 11 ms for 400 rows)
what: Every row write in the filter phase (which shows no per-row progress) is its own WAL commit and fsync.
cost: Measured 927 ms for 400 per-row commits vs 11 ms in one transaction on NVMe; slower on ZFS with sync writes, and 400 write-lock acquisitions contend with select clicks. Once per search.
evidence: Probe against the real schema in a temp DB.
fix: Wrap each filter sub-step in one transaction via a non-committing set_video variant; keep per-chunk enrich commits and committed phase transitions.

title: Each review-grid checkbox click rebuilds the whole grid twice
what: toggle() calls renderGrid() optimistically and again on the reply; renderGrid empties #grid and recreates every visible card with a new img.
cost: Up to 400 cards (~2,400 nodes, 400 images) rebuilt twice per click; estimated 10-40 ms per rebuild; curating 100 clips is 200 full rebuilds with thumbnail re-decodes, on a laptop beside Resolve.
evidence: Read; not measured in a browser.
fix: Update only the clicked card and the footer/header counts; keep renderGrid for filter, chip and bulk changes.

title: Search candidates are kept forever: job_videos / job_video_terms are never pruned
where: ytdl/web/schema.sql:208-258; db.py (no DELETE outside boot recovery, erase, _drop_forgotten_terms)
what: Every candidate of every search stays in ytdl.db after the job is done; nothing reads jobs older than the 20-job Recent list except a deep link.
cost: Measured 356 KB for one 400-candidate job; ~2 searches/day today = ~250 MB/year, ~2 GB/year at 20 editors and ~15 searches/day, in a DB the container holds open and snapshots copy.
evidence: Probe DB size; grep of DELETE statements in db.py.
fix: In the retention pass that item asks for, drop job_videos/job_video_terms of terminal jobs older than N days, keeping the jobs row and never touching the downloads ledger; manifest.json already keeps download provenance.
